LESSON: SIGN READING 11.2.2 COMPREHEN SION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Sign Reading 11.2.2 Comprehen sion
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 11.2.2 Comprehen sion, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we predict how a story, poem or conversation will end? 2. How can we tell where events have taken place?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 11.2.2 Comprehen sion together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: reflection on own is enhanced as the learner relates the events in the text to everyday experiences.

● Creativity and imagination: making connection is enhanced as the learner makes predictions and anticipates possible outcomes in the story using

pictures and title.

Values:
Responsibility: self-drive is enhanced as the learner takes up roles in retelling parts of the story in turns with peers

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (effective communication) is enhanced as the learner talks about where the actions in the story are taking place.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate comprehension of various texts to learning areas in Indigenous Language Activities.
